findings.title: The concept and interview outputs do not obey the Output Conventions
findings.description:
Output Conventions says “Both capabilities write to … `user/analysis/` … with `docType: analysis`,” but Capability 1’s Outputs also places `000-concept.{project}.md` in `user/project-guides/` with `docType: concept`. The delivery rationale therefore covers only the comprehension analysis and overview, not the initiative’s most consequential downstream artifact. Resolve the scope statement and specify the concept’s required metadata (`project`, dates, valid `status`) and its relationship to the existing `001-initiative-plan.squadron.md` source reference (`user/project-guides/001-concept.squadron.md`).

The same boundary omits interview material for Capability 2. Inputs says that, when the concept is absent, purpose comes from “the initiative plan plus interview,” yet `/sq:overview` has no specified interview flow, question boundary, or destination for the answers. It cannot inherit Capability 1’s concept interview by assumption: the optional concept is specifically allowed to be absent. Define where `/sq:overview` obtains Purpose/Audience in that case and how its interview answers remain traceable to an input artifact rather than becoming untraceable authored claims.

findings.title: Sharing the analysis directory can corrupt tech-debt audit measurements
findings.description:
The new `{index}-analysis.codebase-comprehension.md` and `{index}-analysis.overview.md` match the existing metrology harness’s unfiltered `project-documents/user/analysis/*-analysis.*.md` glob. `src/squadron/metrology/audit.py:259-283` selects the newest matching file by mtime, not by `topic: tech-debt-audit`. If an overview or comprehension run writes after an audit starts, that newer file can be selected; it lacks the audit findings block, so the audit is discarded as `BLOCK_MISSING`. More seriously, a generated document written during a later audit can make the harness parse that document rather than the actual fresh audit.

This directly affects the claimed “no change to consumers” integration. The architecture must either reserve a consumer-invisible location/name for these artifacts or include a bounded metrology change that filters by audit topic and rejects multiple fresh candidates explicitly. The 900-band numbering alone does not address this glob collision.

findings.title: Index allocation and output update semantics are unspecified
findings.description:
“Incrementing per run” and “take remaining slots in the 900 band as needed” leave several incompatible implementations: increment independently per directory, per topic, or globally across analysis documents; inspect only `940-949`, or scan all 900-band directories before choosing an index. Those choices produce different results with existing review files such as `940`–`949` in other bands and with future parallel runs. No allocation authority, collision check, or behavior when two generators choose the same index is defined.

Update ownership is also unclear. An overview will need regeneration as initiative statuses change, but the document simultaneously treats analysis runs as independent samples, permits `{index}-analysis.overview.{topic}.md`, and never says whether the default overview is replaced, versioned, or accumulated. Existing squadron review persistence explicitly archives before overwriting; these document generators have no corresponding preservation rule. Define one deterministic allocation rule and whether reruns revise an artifact or create a new sample.

findings.title: The client-overview source contract is incomplete for actual squadron plans
findings.description:
The required input is hard-coded as `001-initiative-plan.{project}.md`, while the concept is optional and all fields have prescribed sources. The real plan has `status: in_progress` while individual completed initiatives also retain that status, and non-started initiatives already contain checked items. The rules “Status is honest” and “no phase numbers or slice indices” do not define how to reconcile plan-level and initiative-level states, checked work, and dates without inventing progress.

Likewise, Roadmap requires “dependency-driven ordering,” but this document does not say whether to parse `Dependencies:` embedded in numbered initiative prose, the separate Cross-Initiative Dependencies section, or both. Those representations can drift. Scope requires “non-goals,” and Risks requires “notes,” but neither is a required section of the stated input. The skill needs an explicit source precedence and missing-source behavior for each such field; “flag the gap” alone does not make Status/Roadmap deterministic enough to implement and test.

findings.title: The external graph contract has no compatibility or validation boundary
findings.description:
The design pins behavior to understand-anything v2.8.1 and requires several exact structures, including `tour[]`, type-prefixed node IDs, and the listed `meta.json` fields, but specifies no version check, schema check, or behavior when an upstream release changes them. Preconditions covers only plugin absence and missing graph. Missing `meta.json`, absent `tour[]`, malformed JSON, missing `nodeIds`, and unsupported versions have no defined failure or degradation behavior, despite the plugin being external and unpinned by squadron.

The read discipline is also incomplete for the stated purpose: Initial Technical Direction is to come from “languages, frameworks, dependencies,” yet Flow step 3 extracts only `project`, layers, tour, and file-level nodes’ summary/path/complexity. It does not identify which node types or edges supply languages/frameworks/dependencies, nor how `.understandignore` coverage limitations constrain those claims. Require a captured v2.8.1 fixture, explicit structural validation with actionable errors, and a defined reduced-output mode for optional sections rather than allowing empty parses to become confident planning prose.

findings.title: Audience handling is specified as both present and deferred
findings.description: Translation rules states “Audience variants share one document” and “Emphasis is a generation parameter.” Resolved Design Decisions instead selects “one neutral document, not per-audience variants” and says an emphasis parameter is added only if real use demonstrates need. The former puts an argument and selectable behavior into the current interface; the latter excludes it. Remove the generation-parameter statement from the current design or explicitly mark it as a future extension, including whether `/sq:overview` accepts any audience argument now.

findings.title: Installation and failure checks need stack-specific preconditions and transactional behavior
findings.description:
Preconditions says to verify that the plugin is installed, but Non-Goals rules out squadron driving Claude Code’s plugin system. No reliable detection mechanism is named; graph existence is separately checkable, but “plugin installed” cannot be inferred from the graph. Define what evidence is checked, or reduce the precondition to the artifacts actually consumed.

Hygiene also needs the target repository root, not merely `$PROJECT_ROOT` in an abstract skill: analysis skills support targets, and editing the wrong checkout’s `.gitignore` would be a side effect outside the analyzed project. Finally, the flow writes `.gitignore`, then interviews, then drafts several artifacts, with no behavior for declined interview, malformed input discovered late, or partial write failure. A subsequent run should not mistake an empty placeholder concept for an approved source. Make the graph/`.gitignore` target explicit and define validation-before-write plus partial-output handling; no rollback machinery is needed, but silently leaving apparently valid partial planning documents is not safe.

structured_findings.summary: The concept and interview outputs do not obey the Output Conventions
Sharing the analysis directory can corrupt tech-debt audit measurements
Index allocation and output update semantics are unspecified
The client-overview source contract is incomplete for actual squadron plans
The external graph contract has no compatibility or validation boundary
Audience handling is specified as both present and deferred
Installation and failure checks need stack-specific preconditions and transactional behavior
